content: This document provides important information about the medication etravirine, which is commonly marketed under the brand name Intelence. It is essential to understand that this information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice, and you should always consult your healthcare provider for complete guidance tailored to your specific health needs. Uses: Etravirine is prescribed in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which allows the immune system to function more effectively. This reduction in viral load decreases the risk of developing HIV-related complications, such as new infections or certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Etravirine is typically prescribed to individuals who have previously used other HIV medications, such as efavirenz, nevirapine, or delavirdine, which were not sufficiently effective in controlling their HIV. Etravirine belongs to a class of drugs known as non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). It is important to note that etravirine is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is crucial to continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. How to Use: Before starting etravirine, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it again each time you receive a refill. Take this medication orally after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually twice daily. Swallow the medication whole. If you have difficulty swallowing the tablet, you may dissolve it in a small amount of water (approximately 1 teaspoon or 5 milliliters). Stir the mixture well until it appears milky. After dissolving the tablet in water, you may add a tablespoon (15 milliliters) of water, orange juice, or milk to the glass and drink the entire mixture immediately. It is critical to take etravirine and other HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Side Effects: Nausea may occur as a side effect of etravirine. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication. These changes may include increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Etravirine may commonly cause a mild rash, which typically appears during the second week of treatment and resolves within 1 to 2 weeks. However, it is important to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare but require immediate medical attention. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada. Precautions: Before taking etravirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby. Etravirine passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding while on this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Your doctor may need to adjust your treatment or monitor you more closely if you are taking certain combinations of HIV medications. Other medications may affect how etravirine is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin and clarithromycin) and rifamycins (such as rifabutin, rifampin, and rifapentine). Etravirine itself may also affect the removal of other medications from your body, which could impact their effectiveness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control assistance. Monitoring and Storage: While taking etravirine, your doctor may order regular lab tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the desiccant (drying agent) in the bottle and tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most up-to-date and personalized advice regarding your treatment.
